acquisition.description: One FRED API series/observations request per configured monthly LAUS county alias (6,282: laus_monthly_unemployment_rate 3,141; laus_monthly_labor_force 3,141), each over the full real-time window 1776-07-04..9999-12-31 so every ALFRED vintage comes back as [realtime_start, realtime_end] spans. Series and their county codes are discovered by build_config.py from FRED release 116 and GeoFRED; the series_id list here must equal config.json (build_config.py --emit-parameters regenerates it). A series FRED does not archive answers 400 "does not exist in ALFRED" and is recorded as skipped. desired_bytes is 1.8 GiB against a declared 2 GiB ceiling for this dataset: 20 sampled full-window payloads measured 174.7 KiB mean for the unemployment rate and 313.7 KiB mean for the labor force, which extrapolates to 1.43 GiB for the two families together.

definition.description: Monthly LAUS county series with every ALFRED real-time vintage: the unemployment rate (FRED alias ...URN) and the civilian labor force (...LFN), 229-264 vintages per series from 2005-06-08 and 2007-06. The county counterpart of fred_county_vintages' annual LAUS averages, whose archive only opens in 2017/2019; the monthly aliases are the only county LAUS source reaching back before 2017. Subjects are geo:US:county:<SSCCC>. Each row carries the vintage it was published in, the units published in that vintage, and whether it is a first release.

sampling.reason: A 100-row excerpt of one series would carry a handful of vintages and could not be told apart from a current-vintage download, which is the exact confusion this dataset exists to remove. pipeline.py refuses to run on anything but the full sharded artifact.
